goal: Prove a high-capability Agent can compose and repair a CapabilityTree while a separate bounded low-cost LLM executor performs file work through the existing Block contract.
delivery_approach: adaptive vertical slice over the stable CapabilityTree, ExecutionDAG, Block, registry, and state authorities
acceptance_criteria: semantic capability versions resolve 1.10 after 1.9 and before 2.0
Growth executor creation uses a generic implementation-identity factory
Agent outputs only validated TreeEdit decisions and is limited to four decisions
cheap LLM outputs strict read/list/write/patch proposals and deterministic code applies them
success, failure-repair, and escalation paths preserve unaffected result reuse
real Provider validation uses different Agent and worker models or readiness remains LEVEL_3

quality_metrics.actual: initial pytest failed; worker patched math_utils.py; final pytest 1 passed

out_of_scope: shell or network tools exposed to the worker
evidence_refs: python -m pytest -q tests/agent tests/capabilities tests/growth tests/executors tests/runtime tests/execution tests/state

feedback: Real high-capability Agent and cheap worker models were separately configured and called.
The worker changed a real file and the existing PythonTestExecutor observed pytest PASS.
Fake-provider tests cover controlled repair, escalation, and forbidden action rejection.

worked: A machine-readable capability catalog prevented model aliases from becoming execution authority.
Fail-closed TreeEdit and empty-DAG validation rejected two malformed real attempts before a successful run.
did_not_work: The first high-model attempt used noncanonical payload aliases; the second used an undeclared structural root.
experiments: Use MVP-014 for a real-provider repair checkpoint and aggregate token/context budget evidence.
